newsitem.title: SPAIN: CiU says Spanish budget backing yields 70 bln ptas.
newsitem.headline: CiU says Spanish budget backing yields 70 bln ptas.

text.p: The Spanish government's Catalan parliamentary allies on Wednesday said they would receive an extra 70 billion pesetas for their region in exchange for backing the minority conservatives' 1997 draft budget.
"There are many issues, from health to special services to our own 30 percent of income tax," Catalan president Jordi Pujol told a radio interviewer.
"This amount is difficult to detail, but I think for 1997 it might be an increase of around 70 billion pesetas," he added.
The Popular Party (PP) depends on the votes of the Catalan Convergence and Union (CiU) coalition for its parliamentary majority.
Pujol added that Catalonia was not the only region to receive extra funds this year. "Many other regional governments will receive this money, not just Catalonia," he said.
The regional coalition previously said it expected to receive an extra 29 billion pesetas next year, but that figure excluded the extra income tax revenue.
Economy Ministry Rodrigo Rato last week said the actual amount of money headed to the autonomous regions was far less that the amount mentioned by CiU.

The draft budget's passage in parliament is assured via the government's votes plus those of its regional allies in Catalonia, the Basque country and the Canary Islands. The final vote on the budget is scheduled for November 22.
